READING

**The numbers in full**

VELLACOTT all-in: GBP 3,050,000 (Suilvenaig) − GBP 610,000 (Brindlemere) + GBP 240,000 (linkspan) = GBP 2,680,000.
TARNSIDE all-in: GBP 1,420,000 (engines) + GBP 310,000 (charter) = GBP 1,730,000.
Extra capital required by VELLACOTT: GBP 950,000.

Annual fuel advantage of VELLACOTT: GBP 190,000.
Simple payback on the extra outlay: GBP 950,000 ÷ GBP 190,000 = **5.0 years**, placing break-even in the autumn of 2031.

That figure is conservative: it counts only fuel and ignores the maintenance differential between a nine-year-old hull and a thirty-one-year-old one.

---

**What TARNSIDE actually buys**

Re-engining solves the single problem the surveyor identified — the engines and gearbox — and nothing else. The hull passes today, but it is already thirty-one years old at the time the work would be done. Every hull survey from 2027 onwards carries the ordinary risk of a vessel of that age. A re-engined Brindlemere will need replacement in some finite number of years; when that point comes you will have had the GBP 1,730,000 spend and still face a vessel-replacement decision. TARNSIDE is deferral, not resolution.

The GBP 310,000 charter is real cost but the timing — January to March, the low-traffic season at five crossings a day — is as good as it gets for a yard period. Sorrelbank having agreed it in principle is a genuine mitigant. This concern is manageable and should not be over-weighted.

The twelve weeks in yard does nothing to reduce the fuel bill. GBP 190,000 a year is a material recurring cost. Over ten years from 2027 that is GBP 1,900,000 in additional fuel alone, nearly matching the total TARNSIDE outlay.

---

**What VELLACOTT actually costs**

The GBP 950,000 extra capital is genuine and not trivial. But it is recovered on fuel alone by 2031, and from that point the advantage accumulates indefinitely on a vessel that will be only about fourteen years old in 2031 versus thirty-six.

The linkspan work at GBP 240,000 is a one-off and an asset improvement to Ardvraich, not pure expenditure.

The Kittiwake valuation holds until 2027-02-11; a November 2026 handover and sale sits comfortably inside that window.

---

**The two genuine problems with VELLACOTT**

**Insurance.** The broker has not quoted. This is the single largest unresolved number in the analysis. If the Suilvenaig attracts materially higher premiums — say GBP 100,000 or more per year — the payback period lengthens significantly and the economics become closer. This figure must be obtained before contracts are signed. It is a condition precedent, not a reason to reject the course.

**Masters.** This is the sharper operational concern. Two of nine will retire rather than take the endorsement. That leaves a rota of seven for a year-round operation doing eleven crossings a day in the busy season. Seven is thin: normal leave, sickness, and the need for rest periods between watches could produce gaps. All seven remaining masters will need to complete the six-week course, which takes each of them off the rota for that period — those cannot all run concurrently without further thinning the cover.

The mitigation is straightforward in principle: begin the endorsement courses on a staggered schedule before handover, and begin advertising for one or two additional masters who already hold or can be sponsored to obtain the endorsement. The 2017 vessel is likely to be more attractive to candidates than a thirty-one-year-old one. The staffing gap is soluble but requires active management starting now, not after handover.

---

**Weighing the two problems against VELLACOTT's advantages**

Insurance: unknowable without a quote, but a newer vessel with a cleaner recent survey history typically attracts competitive premiums, not punitive ones. The risk is real but the prior probability is that it will not overturn the economics. Obtain the quote.

Masters: a temporary operational constraint that can be managed with staggered training and one or two new hires over the winter of 2026-27. It does not affect the long-run position.

Against those two manageable concerns, TARNSIDE offers a permanent GBP 190,000/year fuel drag and leaves Cormorant Sound Ferries operating a vessel that will be in its mid-thirties by the time re-engining costs are recovered — and which will then need replacement with no offsetting sale value at that point, because a 1995 vessel in 2035 is unlikely to fetch GBP 610,000.

---

**Conclusion**

VELLACOTT is the right course. Before committing, two things must happen: get the insurance quote within the next two or three weeks, and draw up a master-endorsement schedule and a recruitment brief so that the staffing position is addressed before handover. Neither of those is a reason to choose TARNSIDE; they are conditions for executing VELLACOTT competently.

CALL
  VELLACOTT

GROUNDS
  The fuel saving alone recoups VELLACOTT's GBP 950,000 extra outlay within five years, after which a 2017 hull continues to compound the advantage on both fuel and maintenance over a 1995 vessel whose underlying replacement cost has merely been deferred by re-engining.
